name: Dry Skin
description: Dry skin lacks sufficient natural oil and moisture, leading to a rough texture and flakiness. It requires special care to maintain hydration and prevent irritation.
characteristics: Fine lines may be more visible
Skin is prone to redness and irritation
recommended_ingredients: Fatty acids (plant oils like jojoba oil, avocado oil)

morning_routine.action: Apply a hydrating cleanser to remove any impurities without stripping the skin.
morning_routine.purpose: Prep the skin for daytime moisture and protect against environmental stressors.

night_routine.action: Use a gentle, non-foaming cleanser followed by an intensive hydrating moisturizer or cream.
night_routine.purpose: Replenish skin's natural moisture barrier while you sleep.

night_routine.action: Apply a nourishing serum rich in hyaluronic acid or ceramides.
night_routine.purpose: Further enhance hydration and support the skin’s lipid layer.

weekly_care: Exfoliate with a gentle chemical exfoliant once a week to remove dead skin cells without causing irritation.
lifestyle_tips: Stay hydrated by drinking plenty of water.
Protect your skin from harsh weather conditions like wind and cold.
common_mistakes: Over-cleansing the skin, which can further strip natural oils.
Skipping moisturizer or using products that are too heavy for daytime use.
do: Apply a humidifier in dry climates to increase indoor humidity.
Use lukewarm water when washing your face rather than hot water.
dont: Skip the sunscreen, even on cloudy days.
Rinse off all cleansers thoroughly and pat skin dry gently with a soft towel.

seasonal_care.summer: Use lighter, oil-free moisturizers to keep skin hydrated without feeling greasy. Protect your skin from sun damage by using a broad-spectrum SPF.
seasonal_care.winter: Increase the use of rich emollients and occlusives to combat dryness. Consider indoor humidification to maintain optimal skin moisture levels.
seasonal_care.monsoon: Protect your skin from increased humidity with gentle, hydrating cleansers and moisturizers that are less likely to cause irritation.

expert_tips: Patch test new products before fully integrating them into your skincare routine to ensure they do not cause irritation.
Consult a dermatologist for personalized advice on managing dry skin, especially if symptoms are severe or persistent.
